A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MorphSeek work, with readable text, equations, tables and figures. The supplied v1 ends with references; v2 additionally contains Supplementary Sections 7–11. The available material supports a reliable document-level comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original registration experiments on OASIS, LiTS and Abdomen MR-CT, including benchmark comparisons, component ablations and efficiency measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and reports additional baseline comparisons, Monte Carlo estimates, sensitivity tests, posterior-collapse measurements and qualitative analyses.

M1.justification: The Gaussian policy heads, deterministic warm-up, Dice/NJD rewards, LDVN scaling, multi-trajectory GRPO and greedy refinement procedure remain. v2 clarifies initialization and supplies implementation details without establishing a changed algorithm or architecture.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate brain MRI, liver CT and cross-modality abdominal registration using the same underlying datasets. The supplementary experiments examine retained coverage; they introduce no new task, population or input environment.

E2.justification: The main comparator set is retained, but v2 adds evaluated LapIRN-diff and LapIRN-disp stage3 baselines on OASIS (Table 7), plus SyN and deedsBCV on all three benchmarks (Table 8). These substantially broaden the reported comparisons beyond citations or promised supplementary results in v1.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 revises v1's assertion of uniform weakly supervised baseline training: v2 allows published protocols for CorrMLP, RIIR, SPAC and WarpDDF+RegCut when unification is unsupported. Added experiments introduce 50-epoch sensitivity tests, classical optimization schedules and alternative SPAC reconstruction procedures. Original pair counts and headline metrics remain unchanged; the revised description does not establish reruns.

E4.justification: v2 adds LDVN scaling ablations, empirical checks of weak dependence, hyperparameter sensitivity, posterior-collapse analysis and a failure case removing image similarity (Sections 7.2–7.6). Section 9 tests SPAC field reconstruction, and Section 11 adds anatomical-label breakdowns and visual comparisons. These substantially extend evidence about stability, mechanisms and failure conditions.

E5.justification: v2 newly reports 20 independent runs for warm-up stability, 1,000-sample Monte Carlo variance estimation, and Dice mean/standard deviation over ten latent samples of one input. It also specifies fixed seeds for label subsampling. Existing Wilcoxon reporting remains, but the relocated efficiency table loses v1's five-run averaging disclosure. These are reporting additions, not evidence that retained experiments received more runs.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and the relocated efficiency measurements retain their numerical values. Substantial new results include LapIRN-diff/disp OASIS Dice of 79.70/84.52, classical baseline scores, sensitivity and collapse outcomes, and SPAC reconstruction results. v2 also reports warm-up success rates of 33% versus 79% and convergence around 120 versus 75 epochs. These are newly reported comparisons, not version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: v1 provides a short affine identity and asserts unbiasedness and linear variance growth. v2 Section 7 adds Proposition 1 with an explicit gradient proof and a covariance-based variance derivation under bounded moments and weak dependence. The mathematical guarantee is narrowed to direction-preserving rescaling, substantially developing and correcting the earlier argument.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the principal registration, label-efficiency and backbone-generality claims. The introduction removes LDVN's 'first general' priority claim and replaces unbiased-gradient assertions with direction preservation and scale control. This is a limited narrowing of one central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations involving hard-case reweighting, preserved stochastic exploration, posterior collapse and reward hacking when anatomical similarity constraints are removed. It also develops the interpolation and composition argument behind withholding SPAC NJD, supported by reconstruction tests. These materially expand mechanisms, failure conditions and qualifications beyond v1's brief discussion.

D1.justification: Section 10 supplies previously unavailable loss implementations, backbone-specific head placement, latent dimensions, clipping bounds, reward/loss weights, temperature annealing, training budgets, checkpoint selection and hardware/software details. Section 8 documents classical baseline configurations. Much of this fills v1's references to an absent supplement; it documents settings without demonstrating that the underlying implementation changed.

R1.justification: v2 adds Heinrich's self-similarity work and Mattes's multimodal registration reference, while removing six dataset/challenge source references, including OASIS, LiTS and Learn2Reg. It also drops the 'first general' LDVN positioning and expands comparisons with classical methods and SPAC. The main related-work narrative remains largely intact.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and section order are retained. v2 condenses dataset descriptions, rewrites baseline-protocol wording, reorganizes LDVN exposition around the supplement and clarifies warm-up discussion. Author information and malformed numerical ranges are corrected. These are localized editorial changes rather than a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the separate title/abstract page with a compact front page and restyles the document. It removes v1's motivational Figure 1, improves labels on the retained qualitative comparison, expands captions and relocates efficiency Table 4 to supplementary Table 11. Seven new tables and four new figures substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important gaps in the supplied v1 by providing LDVN proofs, targeted stability and failure analyses, additional baseline evidence and substantial reproducibility details. Narrowing the unbiasedness claim also improves precision. These gains strengthen support for the central contribution despite unchanged headline scores. Reporting weaknesses remain, particularly the unexplained aggregation of 33%/79% success rates from 20 runs and the lost timing-repeat disclosure, but they do not outweigh the substantial gains.
